question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Minor European Powers – Settlements and Origins]
options: Danish East India Company – Headquartered at Tranquebar on the Coromandel Coast
Ostend East India Company – Chartered by the Austrian Netherlands (Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI)
Swedish East India Company – Headquartered at Canton in China with major territories in Bengal
Prussian Asiatic Company (Emden Company) – Established trade relations primarily with China and Bengal
wrong_fact: The Swedish East India Company never acquired any territorial possessions in India or Bengal. Its trade was almost exclusively concentrated on China (Canton), and it only maintained minor transit/shipping contacts with India.
explanation: The Swedish East India Company, established in 1731, focused almost entirely on the tea and porcelain trade with China (Canton) and did not establish territorial settlements or major factories in Bengal or elsewhere in India, unlike the British, French, or Dutch. The Ostend Company was indeed backed by Austrian Netherlands (under Emperor Charles VI) and established factories at Bankibazar and Covelong. The Danish EIC was headquartered at Tranquebar.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Ostend Company – Settlements and Conflict]
options: Ostend Company – Established a factory at Bankibazar on the Hooghly River
Covelong Settlement – Located on the Malabar Coast of southwestern India
Empress Maria Theresa – Re-established Austrian trade interest later via the Trieste Company
Ban on Ostend Company – Resulted from pressure by the British and Dutch on Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI
wrong_fact: Covelong (where the Ostend Company established a factory) is located on the Coromandel Coast (south of Madras in present-day Tamil Nadu), NOT on the Malabar Coast.
explanation: The Ostend Company (chartered in 1722) established successful factories at Bankibazar (on the Hooghly River, Bengal) and Covelong (on the Coromandel Coast, Tamil Nadu). Due to intense pressure and diplomatic leverage by the British and Dutch, Emperor Charles VI suspended the company's charter in 1727 and dissolved it in 1731. Covelong is on the Coromandel Coast, not the Malabar Coast. Under Maria Theresa, Austria later made attempts through the Trieste Company.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Prussian and Imperial German/Austrian Trade Initiatives]
options: Emden Company (Prussian Asiatic Company) – Chartered by King Frederick II (the Great) of Prussia in 1751
Prussian Company Ships – Used the port of Emden on the North Sea as their home base
Nicobar Islands (Frederiksoerne) – Briefly colonised by Austria in 1778 under the name 'Theresia Islands'
Emden Company – Successfully seized Pondicherry from the French during the Seven Years' War
wrong_fact: The Emden Company (Prussian Asiatic Company) was a small merchant venture that never had the military strength to seize territory and never captured Pondicherry, which was a major French stronghold. Prussian mercantile efforts were purely commercial and short-lived, failing during the Seven Years' War.
explanation: The Prussian Asiatic Company (Emden Company) was established in 1751 by Frederick the Great, operating from the North Sea port of Emden. It focused on trade with Canton and did not possess military forces to capture French Pondicherry. Austria did attempt to colonise the Nicobar Islands (which the Danes had named Frederiksoerne) in 1778, renaming them the Theresia Islands, but abandoned them soon after. Therefore, option 4 is incorrect.
